reviews.author: Mr Vasanth Reddy
reviews.text:
Hello, this is Vasanth Reddy. I’ve been working out at this gym for the past one year, and I want to share my honest feedback.

The gym equipment is in poor condition. Most of the machines are just repainted from old equipment but not properly maintained. I raised a complaint to the management, but there was no response or action taken.

Here are some of the issues I’ve noticed:

1.Abdominal Crunch Machine – damaged and not smooth.
2.Cable Fly Machine in poor condition.
3.Flat Bench Press not stable.
4.No proper labeling on dumbbells.
5.Washrooms are unhygienic with a bad smell and no proper shower.
6.Some weight plates are broken.
7.Tricep V-Bar and Tricep Extension Rope damaged.
8.Hyper Extension Machine not usable.
9.Adjustable/Foldable Bench (Incline/Decline) in bad shape.
10.Air conditioning doesn’t work properly and there’s poor ventilation.

Additional concerns:

No pause or freeze option for membership if you go on vacation.

No general trainers available for guidance.

Trainers only focus on personal training clients and ignore others.

Beginners should be extra careful due to poor equipment and lack of supervision.

Here’s my favorite part — if you try to help a friend with a workout, the management says you’re “spoiling their business.” Seems like fitness is secondary, business first.

Overall, there’s no proper support from staff or management.

I strongly suggest checking the gym and equipment condition in person before taking membership. Based on my experience, I do not recommend this gym.

reviews.author: Abhinav Singh
reviews.text:
Feature Feedback
Equipment ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (Excellent variety and quality)
Trainers ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (Knowledgeable but focused on PT)
Cleanliness ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (Very well maintained)
Value for Money ⭐⭐⭐ (Premium pricing; expensive)
Ambiance ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (Motivating and professional)

Gold's Gym Sarjapur Road is a popular high-end fitness center in Bangalore, often favored for its professional equipment and specialized training. Based on a compilation of member feedback from various platforms like Google, MouthShut, and Reddit, here is a consolidated review of the experience you can expect.
​The Overall Rating: 4.0 / 5.0
​The Positives (What Members Love)
​World-Class Equipment: The gym is highly praised for its range of high-quality machinery. You will find equipment from top brands like Life Fitness and Hammer Strength. The dedicated areas for cardio and spinning are well-designed with "mood lighting" that adds to the workout vibe.
​Knowledgeable Trainers: Many reviewers specifically highlight the trainers (names like Pranay Bane and Sandeep are frequently mentioned) for being motivating and technically sound. They are generally helpful with form and nutrition advice.
​Cleanliness and Hygiene: Hygiene is consistently rated as a priority here. The floors, machines, and locker rooms are regularly cleaned, which is a major plus for most members.
​Diverse Group Classes: For those who don't just want to lift weights, the GGX (Gold's Group Exercise) classes are a hit. They offer Zumba, Yoga, Kickboxing, and HIIT, which are great for breaking up a routine.
​The Drawbacks (Common Complaints)
​Peak Hour Crowds: Like most premium gyms in Sarjapur, it gets very crowded during the morning (7 AM – 9 AM) and evening (6 PM – 8 PM). During these times, you might have to wait for popular machines like the bench press or squat rack.
​Sales Pressure: A common critique is the constant push for Personal Training (PT). Some members feel that the general floor trainers are less attentive unless you sign up for expensive personal coaching.
​Maintenance Lag: While generally clean, there are occasional reports of "dead zones" where the AC isn't functioning perfectly, especially in the cardio section during high-traffic hours.
​Membership & Management: The pricing is on the higher side (ranging from ₹18,000 to ₹50,000+ depending on the plan). Some users have reported that the front desk staff can be rigid or unhelpful regarding membership transfers or refunds.

Hands down, one of the best gyms I’ve visited in India. This facility truly sets a new benchmark in the fitness industry. They have strongman equipment introduced for the first time in India, and most of the equipment is designed and developed in-house, which speaks volumes about their expertise and innovation.

The gym also features a massive 3,000 sq. ft. recovery and rehab zone, including professional physiotherapy, sauna, cold plunge, cryotherapy, infrared therapy, and steam bath—everything an athlete needs for optimal recovery.

What really stands out is the variety of training options under one roof: a Pilates studio, spinning studio, aerial silk training, and even an in-house cafe for post-workout nutrition. The gym is fully equipped with calibrated equipment for powerlifting, octagon cage for MMA, along with dedicated setups for Strongman, Hyrox, CrossFit, bodybuilding, and track & field training.

I have also attended their WPC National Powerlifting Championship in October 2025 and the National Calisthenics Championship on January 9 & 10, 2026. The way these events were organized clearly shows that they are setting new standards in event hosting. More importantly, they genuinely focus on encouraging, supporting, and uplifting athletes and strength sports in India.

Whether you’re a professional athlete or a fitness enthusiast, this place is much more than just a gym—it’s a complete performance and sports ecosystem. Highly recommended!

I had a very bad experience at Cult Fit Sarjapur.

We visited the center after booking a trial class and were interested in taking an Elite membership directly from the center. The center manager, Kothapalli Ashok Kumar Reddy, assisted us and shared a UPI ID named cultfitsarjapur for payment. Although his personal name appeared on Google Pay, we trusted him since he was representing a well-known brand.

Unfortunately, right after the payment was made, he completely ghosted us. Despite multiple follow-ups over two weeks, there was no response from his side.

When we finally visited the center again, we were shocked to learn that he had absconded and scammed around 8–9 people in a similar way.

This is extremely concerning and raises serious questions about internal controls and verification processes at the center. I strongly urge others to avoid making any direct payments to individuals and ensure all transactions are done through official channels only.

Very disappointing experience with what is otherwise a reputed fitness brand.

reviews.author: Himanshu Gupta
reviews.text:
I’ve been training with the cult personal trainer Seben Selvem at Cult Gym, Bellandur for the past 9 weeks and the results have been phenomenal. With his training and balanced diet, I’ve been able to lose more than 5kg of fat while gaining muscle during this time.

At 33, I had never really worked out in a gym beyond occasionally using the treadmill and honestly had an aversion to gym workouts. After reading his Google reviews, I decided to start a 3-month training plan with him, and it has been one of the best decisions I’ve made.

From the very first assessment, Seben has been incredibly encouraging and detail-oriented. He constantly emphasizes correct posture and proper form, even if that means starting with lighter weights. At the same time, he motivates me to push myself and lift heavier when he knows I’m capable. This approach has significantly improved my strength, stamina, and confidence.

My routine usually starts with warm-up run and stretching techniques he taught me, followed by a full hour of structured training and assisted stretching followed by cardio
at the end. Because of this, I’ve rarely experienced soreness or pain—even after intense leg days.

Seben is punctual, friendly, patient, and extremely sincere during training sessions, especially with someone new to strength training like me. I’ve started seeing my body in a much more positive way and have already extended my training with him for another 3 months :)

I would highly recommend Seben to anyone looking for a knowledgeable and dedicated trainer who truly cares about right posture and fitness for you.

reviews.author: Arnab Sen
reviews.text:
Edit 1 (December 9)

I added one extra star because
1. I see more trainers in the floor and they help in spotting.
2. The AC is better regulated nowadays.

What's good
1. Equipment quality
2. General cleanliness
What's bad
1. Lack of availability of equipments compared to the footfall. There is a severe derth of dumbbells. With so many people coming in, a lot more benches and cable-pulley equipments are must.
2. Casette AC in a gym - in specific location it blasts cold air into your head when you are working out. In other areas you feel suffocated because of poor circulation.
What's horrible
1. User etiquettes - no one unracks weights or puts dumbbells back in their place. It's a shame that in a city like Bangalore where highly eductaed individuals are expected to be using the facility, people are so ignorant of basic gym etiquettes.
What's pathetic
1. Not a single trainer on floor. If you don't have any partner you have no one to spot you on request. There is no general trainer and in the afternoon there is just no one. I was surprised that the person at front desk did not even know how to provide spotting for barbell squats. Basically you are on your own.
2. There is no floor manager to keep stuff back in their place. You have to keep hunting for dumbbells and plates.

reviews.author: Nikita Ajit
reviews.text:
I’ve been going to this since it opened this April. Last Saturday, I walk in and it feels like a furnace. The trainers then said that the company had sealed all the air gaps (see image) which were great for allowing fresh air flow through, and did not install ACs, Coolers or anything similar. The large industrial fans obviously just blow HOT air around. The structure is made with a tin roof – now imagine working out inside an overheated metal box!

Any person would immediately understand the health and safety risks of people working out in these conditions. Cult is supposed to have enough experience and knowledge to understand these risks and prep for them. Not seal the air gaps and leave us all to die in here.

For the last 6 days, I have written emails, contacted customer supported 5 times via chat, spoken to the Centre Manager multiple times and various trainers. NOBODY has seemingly done enough to fix the conditions. What authority does the Centre Manager have if he cannot fix this issue – simple solution: remove the boards that are used to seal the air gaps until ACs are installed!

I would avoid coming to the gym until they fix it but I can’t afford to lose my flow. I have a health condition that puts me at high risk for heart attacks, at the same time, working out at the gym is the only way to keep healthy. A double edged sword in the case of Cult Neo Gym Bangalore.

Note 1: I’m sure they will not refund my money if I cancel my annual membership (Cult’s capitalism is unbeatable, hiking prices nearly every month)

Note 2: The fresh air flow was great and it was the thing I liked most about this gym. AC is going to make it like every other gym that stinks of sweat. They tried to solve the problem of mosquitoes, and created a way more dangerous problem. Classic 😅

Edit: In response to the reply from Cult to my review — I have already contacted you via email, in-app chat, phone, and by speaking directly with your staff. It is unfair to ask me to use yet another channel when I have already clearly explained the issue, provided additional context, and suggested possible solutions in my original review.

I urge Cult to take responsibility and implement an appropriate resolution, as this issue was created by your processes, not by me.
